Business Result Advanced · Unit 4

Risk.

Playing it safe, going for it — and everything in between.

quotescollocationslisteningrisk adjectivesreactions
01Warm-up

Two quotes. Do you agree?

Read the quotes. What do they mean? Do you agree or disagree — and why?

Living at risk is jumping off the cliff and building your wings on the way down.
Ray Bradbury, novelist
You can't cross a chasm in two small steps.
David Lloyd George, British Prime Minister (1916–1922)
chasm = a very deep, wide crack in the ground
Reacting to an idea
  • I'm with him on that.…you can't plan everything in advance.
  • I see where he's coming from, but……I'd want at least a parachute.
  • That really resonates with me.…that's exactly how I started my new job.
  • That's easier said than done.…especially when people's safety is involved.
  • That's a bit much.…jumping off a cliff? No, thanks.
  • Hard disagree.…small steps work just fine for me.
14Quick quiz

How risk-averse are you, really?

Choose an answer for each situation — and explain why.

A friend who's a great skier wants to take you down the hardest slope. You've skied three times.

A startup offers you 30% more money. Your current job is stable, and you like your team.

It's Friday, 5:45 p.m. One last task, but the safety check takes 20 minutes.

You get a nice bonus at work. What do you do with it?

Your result:
02Discuss

Are you a risk-taker?

Where are you on the scale? Pick a spot — then explain.

  • 1Do you consider yourself a risk-taker? Why / why not?
  • 2Are you the same person at work and in your free time?
  • 3Tell me about a risk that paid off. And one that backfired.
  • 4Is there a risk you would never take at work? Why not?
Useful phrases
  • I usually play it safe.…I like to know what I'm getting into.
  • I'm not much of a gambler.…I'd rather have a plan B.
  • Sometimes you just have to go for it.…like when I moved to the US.
  • It was a calculated risk.…I'd done my homework.
  • It paid off. / It backfired.…big time.
  • I'd rather not stick my neck out.…unless I'm sure.

05Listening · 4.1

Three people talk about risk. Guess their job.

Listen to each speaker. What do you think they do? What risks do they deal with?

0:00 / 0:00
1

Speaker 1

CEO. Risks: signing big agreements, cutting prices, spending shareholders' money.
2

Speaker 2

Sales rep. Risks: what deal to offer, which leads to follow up — the biggest risk is wasting time.
3

Speaker 3

Risk assessor (an actuary). Risks: health and safety, but also financial, legal, environmental and tech risks.
After listening: which speaker's job is closest to yours? What would you add to what they said?

09Other ways to say it

From "too careful" to "too risky"

All of these words work well — especially in reports, emails and reviews. When you're chatting with colleagues, you can also say:

too carefuljust righttoo risky
over-cautious
risk-averse
"She plays it safe.""He overthinks everything."He won't move without three approvals.
cautious
"She's careful.""He double-checks everything."Better safe than sorry.
sensible
prudent
"Smart call.""That makes sense."She thinks it through first.
bold
"That took guts.""A gutsy move."Risky — but it could pay off.
rash · imprudent
reckless · foolhardy
"He's playing with fire.""That's asking for trouble."He's pushing his luck.

11Reactions

Someone took a risk. How do you react?

Short, natural reactions you hear at work every day. Read them out loud with the right tone.

Surprise

  • No way!She really did that?
  • Wait, what?On his first day?
  • Seriously?Without telling anyone?
  • Get out of here!Sales doubled?

Approval

  • Good call.Testing it first was smart.
  • Smart move.That saved us a ton.
  • That took guts.I couldn't do that.
  • Good for her!She earned it.

Worry

  • Yikes.That could've gone really wrong.
  • Oof, that's rough.Is everyone OK?
  • That's asking for trouble.Someone's going to get hurt.
  • He got lucky.This time.

Doubt

  • Hmm, I'm not sold.Where's the data?
  • That's a big "if".If the supplier delivers…
  • I wouldn't go that far."Reckless" is a bit strong.
  • I see the logic, but……it's still a gamble.
Practice

React — then describe them

Listen to the story. React first — the phrases on the right can help. Then pick the adjective that fits best.

Our plant manager skipped the lockout check to hit the deadline. Nobody got hurt. This time.

Try: "Yikes. He got lucky." · "That's asking for trouble."

Jen wants three more approvals before she'll change the font on a safety poster.

Try: "Seriously? For a font?" · "She overthinks everything."

Our CEO cut prices on the whole server line by 30% overnight. Sales doubled.

Try: "Get out of here! That took guts." · "Good call."

Mark signed a new supplier after one phone call. No site visit, no references.

Try: "Hmm, I'm not sold." · "That's a big if."

Practice

Four more stories

Listen to the story. React first — the phrases on the right can help. Then pick the adjective that fits best.

Before rolling out the new forklift route, Priya ran a two-week pilot on one shift.

Try: "Smart move." · "Better safe than sorry."

Our team lead won't try any new software. "If it ain't broke, don't fix it," he says.

Try: "I see the logic, but…" · "He plays it safe."

A new hire climbed a shelf without a harness to grab a box. On his first day.

Try: "Wait, what? On his first day?" · "He's playing with fire."

Dan quit his stable job to open a coffee truck. He'd saved for two years and tested the menu at weekend markets first.

Try: "Good for him!" · "Bold — but smart. It was a calculated risk."

13Speaking

Think of someone you know

A colleague, a friend, a family member. How do they deal with risk? Are they like you?

  • 1Who is the biggest risk-taker you know? What did they do?
  • 2Who is the most careful? Does it ever drive you crazy?
  • 3Who would you want next to you in a crisis — and why?
  • 4How are they similar to you? How are they different?
Useful phrases
  • She's the type who……reads the fine print twice.
  • He tends to……jump in first and ask questions later.
  • Compared to me, she's way more……laid-back about deadlines.
  • We're total opposites when it comes to……money.
  • It drives me crazy when he……skips the safety briefing.
  • I'd trust her with my life.She never panics.
